description: Derived controlled-language dictionary for the LAAS healthcare profile. The markdown tables in healthcare.md section 3 are authoritative; this file is derived from them. Each term carries exactly one approved meaning and one part of speech (STE-C-04). No term appears in both the nouns list and the verbs list. Entries in forbidden with class 'notation' are blocking at every Consequence Tier, including CT0 (healthcare.md section 5.2, deviation 1).

nouns.meaning: The set of medication orders currently in effect for one patient.
A recorded harm to a patient that followed the administration of a medication.
A record of one substance, the reaction it caused in this patient, and the severity.
The documented set of planned interventions for one patient over a stated period.
A system-generated warning presented to a clinician before an order is signed.
A set of patient records selected by a stated rule for analysis or export.
The record of a patient's documented permission for a stated use of their data or their care.
A stated condition under which a medication or a procedure must not be used.
A medication subject to statutory prescribing and dispensing controls.
A data set from which direct and indirect patient identifiers have been removed by a stated method.
The destination and care setting to which a patient is released from an encounter.
The amount of a medication given at one time, stated as a numeral and a unit.
The amount of a medication given per unit of time, stated as a numeral, a unit, and a time unit.
A stated effect that occurs when two named medications are given together.
A patient record that a matching process asserts refers to the same person as another record.
One episode of care with a start time, an end time, and a care setting.
The list of medications approved for use at an institution.
The numeric confidence that two patient records refer to the same person.
The stated clinical reason for which a medication or a procedure is ordered.
A measured value from a specimen, with a unit, an observation timestamp, and a reference range.
An instruction to supply and give a named medication to one patient at a stated dose, route, and frequency.
The comparison of a patient's active medication list against an external medication list, with each difference explained.
The smallest field set sufficient for a stated purpose.
A predefined group of orders applied together for a stated clinical situation.
The unique identifier of one patient within a named identifier system.
The complete set of records held about one patient under one patient identifier.
The set of active diagnoses recorded for one patient.
Patient data that identifies a person and relates to their health, care, or payment for care.
The operation that combines two patient records under one patient identifier.
The interval of values considered expected for a stated population and specimen type.
The path by which a medication enters the body, stated by an approved route term.
The time at which a dose is planned to be given.
The recorded seriousness of a reaction, stated by an approved severity term.
The biological sample from which a laboratory result is produced.
A payer's recorded decision to cover a stated treatment.
The urgency classification assigned to a patient at presentation, from a named triage scale.
A measured physiological parameter, with a value, a unit, and an observation timestamp.

verbs.meaning: Give a dose to a patient. This is a physical act performed by a person.
Withdraw an order before it is acted on.
Stop an active medication order.
Supply a medication from a pharmacy against an order.
Record a clinical observation or a decision in the patient record.
Route a decision to a named clinician or a named queue.
Copy records to a destination outside the treating context.
Attach a recorded marker to a record, an order, or a result.
Combine two patient records under one patient identifier.
Create a medication order or a procedure order for one patient.
Proceed past a clinical decision support alert, with the reason and the responsible clinician recorded.
Authorise a medication for a patient. This is an act by a licensed prescriber.
Compare two medication lists and explain each difference.
Make a result visible to a patient or to a party outside the care team.
Read a record and record a documented conclusion about it.
Set a planned time for an appointment, a procedure, or a dose.
Stop an alert from being presented. This is distinct from override.
Copy an order from one medium into the ordering system without changing it.
Assign a triage category from a named triage scale.
Separate two previously merged patient records. This does not restore the prior state.
Compare a claim against an independent source and record the result.
Omit a scheduled dose, with the reason recorded.

forbidden.reason: Read as zero or four. 4U reads as 40.
Read as IV or as 10.
Read as QID, four times daily.
Read as QD or QID.
Read as morphine sulfate or magnesium sulfate. Different drugs.
1.0 mg is read as 10 mg. Documented tenfold-overdose history.
.5 mg is read as 5 mg. Documented tenfold-overdose history.
Read as u.
Read as mg.
Read as 2.
Read as SL, sublingual.
Read as discharge or discontinue. Opposite actions.
Read as half strength or at bedtime.
Ear and eye abbreviations are confused with each other.
forbidden.replacement: both ears, left ear, right eye, and so on, written in full

forbidden.reason: Describes a rate of change, not a state. A patient can be stably deteriorating.
forbidden.replacement: the measured parameter, the value, the unit, and the interval

forbidden.reason: The clinical sense is the opposite of the everyday sense.
forbidden.replacement: use only as a laboratory result value

forbidden.reason: Statistical and clinical significance are independent.
forbidden.replacement: statistically significant with the test, or clinically significant with the threshold

forbidden.reason: Means sudden onset. A chronic condition can be severe.
forbidden.replacement: sudden onset, or the severity term

forbidden.reason: A disposition decision, or a clinical sign.
Confuses the order with the physical act, and so misstates reversibility.
Means withhold one dose or discontinue the order.
forbidden.replacement: withhold with the dose, or discontinue

forbidden.reason: Means override, suppress, or resolve.
An unmeasured global assessment.
forbidden.replacement: the observed parameters and their values

forbidden.reason: No trigger condition and no maximum.
forbidden.replacement: the trigger condition, the maximum dose, and the minimum interval

forbidden.reason: Self-assessed consequence (ste-core.md section 3.2).
forbidden.replacement: the consequence lattice value from conformance/laas/data.json

forbidden.reason: A room identifies a bed, not a person. Beds change occupants.
forbidden.replacement: the patient identifier and its identifier system

forbidden.reason: States an absence without stating what was examined.
forbidden.replacement: the examined items and the finding for each

forbidden.reason: Impression, not observation (STE-C-10).
forbidden.replacement: the parameter, the two values, and the interval
